items.title: John Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: like I think he was with Jimmy Noone.

ctx.x: Yeah. All you could hear was his voice, and you know, he’d sing like “A Pretty Girl Is Like a Melody,” and these girls would walk around. And you never saw him. And he’d go on the air, like I think he was with Jimmy Noone. And he’d go on the air and sing nothing but ballads you know, just nothing but pretty tunes. But nobody paid any attention to that. A recording company didn’t want to know about that. They didn’t want to record Joe doing any ballads or anything. Right up until the last few years, we had to…

Because when he started out, actually RCA Victor did do some really beautiful things with big bands and strings and things. They never did anything with the records, but you know, this was the era of “A Man Ain’t Supposed To Cry” I think, and some of those things that they did in those days. But they never did anything with them. Because they were pretty ballad things, and they didn’t know how to promote them, they just satisfied Joe, you know.
